source.title: Dynamic computation of incentive salience: "wanting" what was never "liked".

confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration of the exact dissociation MECH-436 names: ventral-pallidum firing to a salt-predicting cue is recomputed upward the instant the animal enters a salt-depletion state, before the salt has ever been tasted as 'liked' -- wanting is modulated by drive state independently of, and even opposite to, the liking history. Rigorous single-unit work in a high-quality venue; discounted for single-axis (sodium) scope and the rat-VP-to-REE transfer.
failure_signatures: The drive-state amplification was selective to the salt cue and immediate (first re-encounter, in extinction, before tasting) -- a REE mechanism that requires re-learning, or that spreads gain non-selectively, would not match.

The effect was demonstrated for a single, strong appetite (sodium depletion driving a large value swing); it does not establish that small or graded multi-axis drive differences produce a measurable wanting shift, which is the regime where V3-EXQ-514q found the effect collapsing.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Ventral pallidum neurons fire only weakly to a cue predicting a previously-disliked intense-salt taste, but fire vigorously to that same cue the first time it is encountered in a novel salt-depletion state -- before the salt is re-tasted and without new learning -- showing that cue-triggered 'wanting' is recomputed in real time by integrating prior Pavlovian associations with the current physiological appetite.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the empirical instance of MECH-436's distinct claim: the homeostatic drive STATE modulates the wanting target/intensity dissociably from liking. The salt cue's 'liking' history is flat-or-negative, yet its wanting amplitude rises with the depletion-axis drive -- exactly 'the most-wanted object tracks the currently-most-depleted drive axis even when the liking/consummatory target does not.'
mapping.mapping_caveat: Single-unit rat ventral-pallidum data for one appetite (sodium). REE's per-object incentive token and per-axis drive are engineered constructs; the paper shows the dissociation EXISTS in biology with a large drive swing, not that a graded, multi-axis, small-spread drive (the V3 regime) suffices to re-rank candidate objects.
mapping.source_context: In-vivo single-unit recording in ventral pallidum of Sprague-Dawley rats; Pavlovian salt-cue under induced sodium-depletion vs normal state; cue-only extinction trials.

confidence_components.notes: Strong empirical anchor for the drive-state-vs-liking dissociation; mapping is faithful but the magnitude/graded-spread question (the substrate-ceiling) is out of scope.
